title: U.S. House · California's 42nd District
area: Long Beach and surrounding Los Angeles County communities, redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Robert Garcia (D) and Republican Brian Burley advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which Garcia received 56.5% of the vote and Burley 20.6%, ahead of two other Republicans and a no-party-preference candidate.

candidates.name: Robert Garcia
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 56.5% of the vote.

priorities.text: Defending democracy, citing support for the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the Freedom to Vote Act.
Raising the minimum wage and expanding the social safety net, including Medicaid, Social Security, Medicare and universal child care.
Expanding pathways to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

positions.summary: Says he will fight for a nationwide $15 minimum wage, citing his push to raise Long Beach's minimum wage to $15 an hour in 2016.
Says he supports Medicare for All and co-chairs Mayors 4 Medicare, and will fight to protect and expand Medicaid, Social Security and Medicare in Congress.
positions.quote: I believe the best approach to fixing our healthcare system is passing Medicare for All.

positions.summary: Says he strongly supports the Green New Deal and will fight to transition away from fossil fuels, citing Long Beach's fleet electrification and green-jobs programs under his mayoralty.

Says he will fight to expand pathways to citizenship for undocumented residents and end legal discrimination against them, citing his work establishing a legal defense fund and sanctuary-city protections in Long Beach.
Says every parent should be able to afford child care and that he will fight for universal child care and pre-K in Congress.
His official site says he believes Congress must enshrine the right to an abortion into federal law.
positions.quote: Congress must enshrine the right to an abortion into Federal law

positions.summary: His official site says he wants Congress to pass universal background checks, an assault-style weapons ban, a minimum age of 21 for gun ownership, a federal licensing system and red flag laws.
positions.quote: legislation that mandates universal background checks for all firearm purchases, bans assault-style weapons, prohibits gun ownership by those under the age of 21 and establishes a strong federal licensing system

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 8085, the Ultra-Millionaire Tax Act of 2026, a bill to impose a tax on the net value of assets of a taxpayer (119th Congress).

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, the Committee on Homeland Security, and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for the 2025-2026 term.

candidates.name: Brian Burley
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 20.6% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: Member, Huntington Beach City School District board (since 2024)

priorities.text: Says he will advocate for tax relief for families and business owners, take a stand against illegal immigration, fully support law enforcement and the military, and work to restore what he calls American family values.

Says his approach as a school board member — protecting parents' voices and stewarding taxpayer dollars responsibly — is the servant-leadership style he would bring to Congress, focused on safe neighborhoods, quality education and a strong economy.

candidates.researchNotes: Campaign website lists four pledges and a 'why I am running' statement; no issue pages or 2026 Ballotpedia survey found. A 2019 survey for a run in a different district is not cited as stale.

statements.quote: Take a Stand Against Illegal Immigration
statements.context: On his campaign website's list of what he will do as Congressman
